title: Rethinking the Hyperparameters for Fine-tuning
mechanism: Optimal effective lr and momentum for fine-tuning depend on source-target similarity; reference-based regularisation can fail for dissimilar datasets.
adaptation: Run the never-run grid: encoder lr {1e-4,3e-4,1e-3} x decoder lr {1e-3,3e-3} x beta1 {0.9,0.95}, on module-grouped 5-fold CV. Also warns that EL is dissimilar to ImageNet, so L2-SP / SPD may need small lambda.
evidence: Extensive transfer benchmarks (classification); momentum and effective lr matter; regularisation toward init not always helpful on dissimilar data.
min_experiment: 12 cells x 5 folds x 2 seeds vs house and PF cells. Metric: CV crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU. Kill if best cell is within CV noise of PF.
prior_overlap: none. lr fixed at 1e-3 Adam (PF 0.1x on encoder) in every run so far.

alt_notes.adaptation: Grid never run: optimizer {Adam + L2 (house), AdamW} x encoder lr {1e-3, 3e-4, 1e-4} x layer-wise lr decay {1.0, 0.7} on module-grouped 5-fold CV, 2 seeds per cell, decoder lr fixed at 1e-3.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: 12-cell grid on CV, best cell rerun 5 seeds. Baseline: house and SUP100-PF. Metric: CV crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU, then test and E1. Kill: best cell within 0.012 crack relF1@2 and 0.02 inactive IoU of PF.
